title: Linux Node Temporal Authority
objective: Pin Rust 1.86 for both Linux architectures, force Node 26.7 Temporal support, and bind/prove the exact toolchain in baseline and SEA receipts

handoff.summary: Integrated the pinned and verified official Rust 1.86.0 Linux x64 and arm64 distributions, enabled Temporal in the reproducible Node 26.7.0 manylinux build, proved Temporal in the build container, UBI 8 runtime, and an assembled SEA, and bound the Rust authority into baseline receipts, both SEA build identities, and Linux candidate validation.
risks: The broad portable tier initially failed because the fresh worktree lacked optional FLINT addons, FLINT headers, and generated runtime/module caches; after the ordinary bootstrap restored those products, all 430 portable tests passed. Both receipts are retained as environmental history.
Native x64 and arm64 Node-stage proofs are release artifact gates and are still running independently on their respective machines.
The final all-inputs Linux builds must be repeated from the frozen release commit so their receipts and executable manifests bind that exact source revision.
next_steps: Integrate this source authority after independent review.
Retain the x64 and arm64 native Node-stage receipts as platform evidence.
Run the all-inputs baseline and candidate packager on both native Linux architectures after the release source commit is frozen.
